newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Union Bank unit seeks seat at Manila bourse.
newsitem.headline: Union Bank unit seeks seat at Manila bourse.

text.p: UBS Securities (East Asia) Ltd, the stock brokerage arm of the Union Bank of Switzerland, said on Thursday it is planning to buy a seat at the Philippine Stock Exchange.
UBS Securities vice-president Corazon Guidote said in a briefing the firm hopes to buy a seat within the next 12 months.
At present, the firm is limited to selling local securities to foreign fund managers.
Guidote said UBS is finalising its staff requirements and waiting for a reduction in the price of an exchange seat before buying one.
A seat on the Philippine Stock Exchange now costs 65 million pesos to 70 million pesos, lower than the maximum price of 75 million pesos earlier this year.
At present, the Philippine stock exchange has 186 members, 176 of whom are active and over 40 are foreign brokers.
UBS research head Norman Villamin said the firm was finalising its investment strategy for the Philippines.
Villamin said this will likely feature an upgrade on the rating for the banking sector due to the improving macroeconomic scenario.
Earlier, UBS recommended a sell due to concerns over the asset quality of banks and low provisions for bad debts as a percentage of total loans.
